senses.gloss:
Sthūṇā in the Rigveda and later denotes the ‘pillar’ or ‘post’ of a house.
Foot notes i. 59, 1; v. 45, 2; 62, 7; viii. 17, 14; x. 18, 13 (of the grave).
Av. iii. 12, 6 (of the vaṃśa, ‘beam,’ being placed on the pillar); xiv. 1, 63; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, xiv. 1, 3, 7; 3, 1, 22, etc.; sthūṇā-rāja, ‘main pillar,’ iii. 1, 1, 11; 5, 1, 1.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 153.

Sthūri has in the Rigveda and later the sense of ‘drawn by one animal’ instead of the usual two (see ratha), and always with an implication of inferiority.
Foot notes x. 131, 3.
taittirīya brāhmaṇa, i. 8, 2, 4; iii. 8, 21, 3; pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa, xvi. 13, 12; xviii. 9, 7; aitareya brāhmaṇa, v. 30, 6; Satapatha brāhmaṇa, xiii. 3, 3, 9, etc.
